There are real differences. `structuredClone` keeps Dates, Maps, Sets, typed arrays and `undefined` values and handles circular references. The JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, Maps and Sets into `{}`, drops `undefined` and functions, and throws on circular references. `structuredClone` throws on functions and can't clone class instances' prototypes (you get plain objects), so neither is perfect, but `structuredClone` is the right default unless you want JSON semantics.
Action: If you paste the line the reviewer flagged, I'll tell you whether swapping it is safe for that data.

Middleware runs before every matched request, so Next designed it to be fast and globally deployable, which is why it defaults to the Edge runtime: lightweight V8 isolates, quick cold starts, but no Node APIs like fs. The tradeoff is that some Node-only libraries won't work. Newer Next versions may let you opt into the Node runtime, so I'd check whether ours does.
Action: Check the Next version in apps/web/package.json and whether anything in middleware.ts needs Node APIs.
